cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Prove the 3-day rhythm and calibrate every main pattern — hinge, squat, pull, single-leg — on straight sets, baselines from the bar, not the résumé.
Install the four-site tendon armour your job never gives you — elbow, shoulder, knee and Achilles — plus the posterior-chain and scapular base everything else builds on.

paragraphs: Mehdi, you told me you want to lift heavy and keep your joints safe while you're on court 7 or 8 hours a day. That's exactly what we're building. But we don't start heavy. This first month is about finding your real numbers on four lifts, and putting some armour on the joints your job hammers every single day.
Your job for these 4 weeks is simple. Show up 3 times, log honestly. The weights will feel easy at first and that's on purpose, because I need to see how you move before we load you up.
By the end of the month you'll know your working weights, the holds will stop feeling strange, and you'll be ready for month 2 when the loads start climbing.
outcomes: Working weights found on all 4 main lifts
Squat and RDL owned at the full 3-second tempo
Both calf holds up to 35 seconds
Protein target hit on training days

cycles.name: Tendon Bank
focuses: Heavy-slow-resistance loading at 5–8 reps on the calibrated lifts, loads climbing weekly from logged RPE — connective tissue built under real load before the heavy block.
Single-leg robustness plus the isometric minimum as session bookends; a programmed back-off closes the cycle.

paragraphs: Next month the loads start climbing for real. Same four lifts, just slower and heavier, and that's where tendons actually get tough.
The joint work doubles too. Twice the attention on knees, elbows and shoulders, because month 3 is when the bar gets properly heavy and I want you ready for it.
Nothing new to learn. Just more of what you'll already own.
You find the numbers now. Next month we grow them.

cycles.name: Payday
focuses: First genuinely heavy block — top sets of 5 at RPE 7–8, tiny set counts, long rests, on lifts practiced for 9 weeks.
Isometrics and posterior-chain accessories at maintenance minimum; heavy lower days never sit next to your heaviest court days.

cycles.name: Double Down
focuses: The same lifts progressed to triples at RPE 8 — never a grinder, never a tested max; the second heavy exposure is where your numbers actually move.
Upper-limb armour — elbow, wrist, shoulder — takes the featured accessory slot.

cycles.name: The Keeper
focuses: Heavy anchors held at full intensity, half the volume — the permanent year-round rhythm, stress-tested against your worst court weeks.
Weak-link audit and e1RM re-check from six months of logs — the isometric minimum becomes the for-life floor.

days.completionMessage: Squat's in the log and your knees just picked up some armour. Get some food in you and stay off your feet if you can.

good: Smooth circles, light sweat by the end
Legs waking, breathing stays conversational
bad: Don't race it — it's a ramp, not a workout

good: Push the floor away with your heels
Glutes lifting, not lower back
Tear the band apart to your chest
Shoulder blades squeezing together
Light kettlebell — sit between your heels
Hips and ankles opening, weight mid-foot
bad: Don't let the elbows drop inside the knees

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: You've got no numbers on file yet, so start lighter than you think and build up over the first two sessions. Keep the lowering to 2 seconds this week, then go to the full 3 seconds from week 2. Only settle at the harder RPE once the bar is still moving well.

good: Push the floor apart
Quads and glutes loading through the whole descent
bad: Don't let the knees cave in

good: Pull the dumbbells to your hips
Shoulder blades drawing down and together

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.note: Only a few sets here on purpose. Your shoulders already work overhead all day on court, so this keeps the pattern going without adding to that load.

good: Press straight up without leaning back
Delts working, neck relaxed
bad: Don't arch the lower back off the pad

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.note: Put a plate or a dumbbell on your lap once you're steady in the position. Bodyweight alone is too easy for you and won't do the job. The last 10 seconds should be a real fight.

good: Press the floor through mid-foot, back flat on the wall
Quads burning evenly, kneecaps tracking straight
bad: Don't slide your hands onto your thighs

exercises.name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
exercises.note: Use the machine rather than holding dumbbells, so your hands are free and the hold stays rock steady. One long hold at mid height, not reps.

good: Push tall through the balls of the feet and freeze
Calf and Achilles loaded and steady

days.completionMessage: Hamstrings, glutes and back did the work today, and that's the stuff that keeps you moving well on court. Eat properly tonight.

good: Long smooth strokes
Hips hinging each stroke, back long
Push hips back into the band
Hamstrings stretch-loading
Arch and round slowly through the full range
Each segment of the spine moving
Pull the shoulder blades down without bending the elbows
Lats setting the shoulders

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.note: Start light and let the hinge feel right first. Just below the knee is plenty of range for now. Use straps from week 2 onwards, because your grip is never meant to be what stops this lift. Your hands get plenty of work on court.

good: Push the hips back to the wall behind you
Hamstrings loading like cables
Drive the elbows down to the ribs
Lats doing the pull, not the biceps
bad: Don't lean far back and heave

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.note: If your gym has no landmine attachment, just wedge the bar into a corner. This angle is much kinder on a shoulder that works overhead all day.

good: Press up and slightly forward along the bar's arc
Delts and upper chest sharing the work

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.note: Keep your elbow pinned to your ribs and hold completely still. Staying strict matters more than using a strong band. We'll go heavier later in the month once you own the position.

good: Pin the elbow to the ribs, press the band out and freeze
Back of the shoulder holding, blade set down
Push the floor away, one long line head to feet
Side of the trunk and glute holding you up

days.completionMessage: Single leg work is the closest thing in the gym to what you actually do out there. That's your week finished, well done.

good: Smooth circles, light sweat by the end
Legs waking, breathing stays conversational
bad: Don't race it — it's a ramp, not a workout

good: Step back onto a rail, drop straight down
Front leg owning the balance
bad: Don't push off the back foot

good: Push the ground away sideways
Side of the hips burning
bad: Don't let the knees collapse inward

good: Drive the heel down, hips to the ceiling
One glute doing all the work

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.note: Balance is what will limit you in week 1, not strength. Start with bodyweight or very light dumbbells and let the depth come as your balance settles.

good: Drive the floor away through the front mid-foot
Front-leg quad and glute doing all the work
Hinge down, then squeeze tall through the hips
Glutes and hamstrings lifting, not the lower back
bad: Don't hyperextend past a straight line

good: Pull the rope to the eyebrows, elbows high and wide
Rear delts and between the blades working
bad: Don't turn it into a row

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Extension
exercises.note: This one's for your elbow, from all the balls you feed every day. Light dumbbell, hold it dead still, and lower it slow at the end. Don't rush this.

good: Knuckles up to the ceiling, hold dead still
Top of the forearm near the elbow working
bad: Don't let the wrist collapse fast

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
exercises.note: Rest the dumbbell on your knee and just steady it with your hand. Bent knee hits the deeper calf muscle, which is the one your court movement actually runs on.

good: Heels up, freeze at mid-height
Deep calf working behind the shin

cards.title: Why Only 3 Short Sessions
cards.body:
You might look at this program and think it's not much. 3 sessions, 45 minutes, weights that feel light. That's deliberate.

You already train more than almost anyone I coach. 7 or 8 hours on court every day is a massive amount of work for your legs and your shoulder. The last thing you need from me is more tiredness.

Court gives you thousands of quick, light movements. What it never gives you is heavy slow loading, and that's the thing that makes tendons and muscle tough. So that's all the gym does for you. Short sessions, low volume, and we push the weight instead of the hours.

cards.title: How To Pick Your Weights
cards.body:
The app never tells you a weight. You find it yourself using the RPE number on each exercise. RPE is just how hard the set felt out of 10. RPE 6 means you could have done about 4 more reps if you had to.

For a lift you've never done, start lighter than you think. Do the first set, then decide:

  • Felt easier than the target? Go up a bit on the next set.
  • Felt about right? Stay there and log it.
  • Felt harder than the target? Drop the weight straight away, not next week.

Week to week it's the same idea. Hit all your reps at or under the target RPE, add a small jump next session. Missed reps or it felt like a grind, stay on the same weight and do it again.

And listen, going lighter is not failing. Some days you'll have coached 8 hours and slept badly. Dropping the weight on those days is the smart move. I'd rather see an honest log than a hero one.

cards.title: Week 1 Will Feel Strange
cards.body:
The squat and the RDL have a slow lowering phase, 2 seconds this week and 3 seconds from week 2. Your legs and hamstrings probably aren't used to that, so expect some stiffness for a day or two after the first sessions.

That stiffness is normal and it fades. It shouldn't stop you working on court. If it does, or if something feels sharp instead of just stiff, message me and we'll pull the weight back.

This is exactly why week 1 is light. I'd rather you feel a bit stiff than wreck yourself before a full coaching day.

cards.title: Don't Skip The Boring Holds
cards.body:
The wall sit, the calf holds, the shoulder and wrist holds. They look like nothing. They're the reason you'll still be coaching pain free in 5 years.

Your knees, achilles, shoulder and elbows take a beating every day on court. Long hard holds are what actually thickens a tendon up and makes it handle that load. Fast reps don't do it, and you get plenty of fast on court already.

So treat them like real sets. Dead still, full time, and heavy enough that the last 10 seconds are a fight. If a hold feels easy it isn't working.

cards.title: Protein Is Your Muscle Insurance
cards.body:
You said your eating is a bit up and down. That's the one thing that can quietly undo all of this, because you're burning a lot of calories on court before you even touch a weight.

Aim for around 120 to 150g of protein a day. For you that's about 4 solid portions. Eggs or yoghurt in the morning, meat or chicken with two meals, something quick after training.

Don't worry about the rest of the diet yet. Just protein, every day, and tell me at the check-in how it's going. If you keep your muscle on 3 short sessions a week, protein is doing most of that job.

cards.title: When The Week Falls Apart
cards.body:
You told me your weeks are heavy and stretched. Some of them will beat you. That's normal and I've already planned for it.

On a bad week, do 2 sessions instead of 3. In each one do the first main lift plus one back or hamstring exercise, then go home. That counts as a full week in my book.

What I don't want is you binning the whole week because you couldn't do it properly. 2 short sessions keeps everything moving. Zero is what sets you back.

cards.title: Your Sleep Is Your Edge
cards.body:
One thing on your form stood out. You rated your sleep 10 out of 10 at 7 to 8 hours a night. That's genuinely rare and it's a big reason I think this plan will work for you.

Most people I coach are fighting bad sleep on top of a busy life. You're not. It means your body can actually absorb the work, even with your court hours.

Protect it. It's doing more for your recovery than any supplement or stretch ever will.
